title: High-volume morning session momentum: 08-16 UTC surge carried to 23:00 UTC
rule_summary: Closed 1h candles, UTC clock, signal at bar close, order at next bar open. Per pair, one position. Session return S = close of the 15:00 UTC bar / open of the 08:00 UTC bar - 1 (8 bars). Session volume SV = sum of volume of those 8 bars; VrefS = mean of SV over the previous 20 calendar days. ENTRY at the close of the 15:00 bar (buy at 16:00 open) when S >= 0.015 AND SV >= 1.5 * VrefS AND the close of the 15:00 bar is above the SMA(200) of 1h closes AND the 15:00 close is in the top 25% of the 8-bar session range (close - session low)/(session high - session low) >= 0.75. EXIT: close of the 22:00 UTC bar (sell at 23:00 open) or earlier if a closed bar is 1.5% below the entry price. No re-entry the same day. Lookbacks: 8 bars, 20 days (480 bars), 200 bars.
mechanism: Shen, Urquhart and Wang find early-session Bitcoin returns predict later returns, strongest in the highest volume or volatility sessions, which they attribute to liquidity provision: dealers absorbing a large one-sided flow must rebalance later, pushing price further. Wen et al. (Intraday return predictability in crypto: momentum, reversal, or both) report reversal as well as momentum, and that large jumps change the pattern, so the high-volume and close-near-high filters aim at the momentum regime. Counterparties are liquidity providers and late fading traders. A 1.5% session surge leaves room for a continuation move above the 0.30% round trip, but the evidence is the abstract-level and equity-style daily clock adapted to 24/7 crypto, so it is untested.
